models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Benign and light through tomorrow at Portorosa - the weather to plan around is the WNW build late on the 10th into the 11th.
briefing.synopsis: No organised gradient over the Aeolians: winds are light and direction-variable, swinging S through N and back with the diurnal cycle rather than any front. At Portorosa the consensus sits at 3-6 kt through tonight and tomorrow (ECMWF IFS and AIFS, both 09 Oct 06Z; ICON-2i 12 Oct... 09 Oct 12Z), with seas under 2 ft. From late on the 10th a WNW flow fills in across the archipelago - Portorosa 11.2 kt WSW at midnight on the 11th and 11.5 kt WNW at 06:00 with 4.2 ft total sea, and the outer islands worse (Salina and Filicudi 5.2 ft, Lipari 5.3 ft at 06:00 on the 11th). I do not have a surface pressure analysis in the payload, so that is inference from the wind field only.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: Portorosa Marina, as recommended - an enclosed basin with all-round shelter, scored sheltered. Overnight figures are 4.7 kt SE, gusts 12.8 kt, 0.9 ft WNW swell. Note the models disagree on the midnight wind at Portorosa, spanning 1.2 to 9.8 kt, but at either end of that range it is a quiet night alongside. Nothing in the payload would push the fleet to move.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Tomorrow stays light at the berth: 4.2 kt SW, gusts 12.8 kt, 1.0 ft WNW swell, with Portorosa hourly data showing 5.8 kt ESE at 06:00 (1.6 ft sea) and 5.5 kt WNW at midday - though the midday spread across models runs 1.7 to 12.0 kt. The payload lists only one leg with a forecast, Salina to Portorosa, 24 nm on 156 degrees true, dated 09 Oct, with a recommended 06:00 departure and every window from 06:00 to 14:00 verdicted go on winds of 4-8 kt and seas 0.8-1.0 ft. If that leg is still ahead of you, the whole 06:00-14:00 band is open and it is a motoring or light-reaching day; I have no forecast for any leg beyond it. The berth recommendation for 10 Oct is Portorosa again.

passage_notes.note: All five windows 06:00 through 14:00 rated go. 06:00 gives 4.3 kt S - head to wind, motor. 08:00 gives 4.9 kt E close reach; from 10:00 it backs N then NE at 6-8 kt for a run or broad reach. Seas 0.8-1.0 ft throughout. Gusts of 20-26 kt appear against 4-8 kt means - these are ECMWF IFS interval-maximum values in light air, reported but not treated as a caution.

cautions: Model spread is wide at several hours: Portorosa midnight tonight 1.2-9.8 kt and midday tomorrow 1.7-12.0 kt. Plan for the top of the range, not the mean.

Gust fields are unreliable in this light air - Stromboli shows 65.1 kt at 06:00 on the 10th against a 6.4 kt mean, and Salina 42.4 kt against 9.3 kt. These are interval-maximum artifacts from a single model, not a forecast of squalls, but they do mean the gust column should not be read literally tomorrow.

Looking past tomorrow: a WNW build late on the 10th into the 11th brings 4.2 ft at Portorosa and 4.5-5.3 ft at Salina, Lipari, Panarea, Filicudi and Stromboli by 06:00 on the 11th, with winds 12-17 kt. Worth building into any plan to leave the marina on the 11th.
briefing.confidence_note: The models agree closely on magnitude - mean wind shift between runs is 1.8 kt at 12-24 h - but direction is genuinely volatile, with a mean 71-degree shift at that lead time and 6-plus knot spreads at several hours, so the speeds are trustworthy and the wind angles much less so.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
